name: Green Isle

attributes.attribute: one of the Fortunate Isles of Scotland
part of Fairyland with orchards of magical fruit
also called the Isle of Apples
imagined as home only to women

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Green Isle is a Scottish mythological site and one of the Fortunate Isles. It belonged to Fairyland and grew orchards of magical fruit, most often apples. Some people called it the Isle of Apples. Storytellers imagined the Green Isle as a place that held only women.

okr.objective: Describe the Scottish Green Isle as a fairy isle of apples lived in by women.
key_results: Green Isle counts among the Fortunate Isles.
Its orchards grew magical fruit, especially apples.
Some call it the Isle of Apples, a land of women.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2003
